title: THE DRAFTER EMITS NO-OP EDITS ON ABOUT A THIRD OF WALK EDIT ATTEMPTS. MEASURED 2026-09-05 across the full goal-host jour
description: THE DRAFTER EMITS NO-OP EDITS ON ABOUT A THIRD OF WALK EDIT ATTEMPTS. MEASURED 2026-09-05 across the full goal-host journal: of 277 'walk rawResolve fs_edit' lines, 98 fail with 'oldString and newString are identical — no edit needed'. That is roughly 35 percent of edit attempts in which the drafter proposed a change that changes nothing — the single largest failure mode, ahead of path errors (28), file-not-found (5) and anchor-miss (4). CORROBORATED FROM THE OPERATOR SIDE IN THE SAME SESSION: a one-statement change to rhythm-conductor-tick.ts line 72 was attempted three times with escalating specificity and refused three times — first as 'old_string and new_string are identical — this op is a no-op, not an edit', then on TS2339 when only one of two required casts was widened, then by the semantic gate with refuters agreeing 2/2 that res was still not cast. Even a goal naming both required casts and explaining why did not produce a correct patch. WHY THIS IS THE AUTHORING CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A NUISANCE: every no-op consumes a compose slot in a lane that admits one attempt at a time (tracked as compose-throughput-is-one-lane-against-a-growing-pool). A third of the scarcest resource is spent producing nothing. Note the guard itself is GOOD — fs_edit refuses identical strings rather than committing an empty change, which is the same class of check that is MISSING further downstream, where a compiling-but-inert patch passes every gate. FALSIFIER: closed only when the identical-strings share of walk fs_edit attempts falls materially below the measured 98 of 277 — cite a journal window with both counts. A closure citing a single successful edit is fabricated, because the defect is a rate.
